Electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) is a technique used to detect protein–DNA interactions by observing changes in the mobility of DNA fragments during gel electrophoresis when bound by proteins.  
Western blotting detects proteins, Northern blotting detects RNA, and Southern blotting detects DNA, but none of these directly demonstrate protein binding to specific DNA sequences in the way EMSA does.
